name: EditorLayout
summary: An editor: a bar across the top, a panel at each side that can be hidden, and the working area between them that takes the rest of the room. For a design tool, a diagram or map editor, a page builder. In a narrow window an open panel floats over the working area from its own edge. Not for a list beside a document (ListDetail) or a conversation (ChatLayout).
a11y: Each panel is a labelled `aside` its toggle controls (`aria-expanded`), in the bar or, without a bar, at the working area's top corners; the bar is the `header`; the working area (the `main` landmark) follows the start panel in the source, and the floating tools bar (a labelled region) follows the working area. Each panel scrolls on its own, with the library's overlay scrollbar (ScrollArea), never sideways. In a narrow window a floating panel closes with Escape and returns focus to its toggle. With `resizable`, each docked panel's handle is a focusable `separator` with the panel's width as its value, controlling the panel.

keys.action: narrower or wider by a step (`resizeStep`, 8 px), four with Shift
back to the opening width (a double click too)

props.name: bar
props.description: The bar across the top, between the two panel toggles: the file's name, who's here, zoom, Share. Leave it out for a design tool's frame with no header (Figma UI3): put those in `startHead` and `endHead`, and the panel toggles float at the working area's top corners.

props.name: startHead
props.description: The start panel's own header, above its scrolling content and never scrolled away: the file's name and menu.

props.name: endHead
props.description: The end panel's own header: who's here, zoom, Share.

props.name: start
props.description: The panel at the start: layers, pages, assets.

props.name: startLabel
props.description: Names the start panel and its toggle: "Layers" (default).

props.name: end
props.description: The panel at the end: the selection's properties.

props.name: endLabel
props.description: Names the end panel and its toggle: "Properties" (default).

props.name: tools
props.description: The tools (move, frame, shapes, text, comment): a bar that floats over the working area, centred at its bottom (Figma UI3), never in the header.

props.name: toolsLabel
props.description: Names the floating tools bar's region: "Tools" (default).

props.name: children
props.description: The working area between the panels, usually a Canvas. It fills the room left and scrolls on its own.

props.name: height
props.description: `fill` takes the height its parent gives it; `screen` the whole window (an app on its own); `lg` holds 36 rem (a demonstration).

props.name: resizable
props.description: Each docked panel gets a handle on its inner edge to drag it wider or narrower, between `c.editor-layout.panel-min` and `panel-max` (a design tool's panels). `start` or `end`: only that panel (an inspector beside a fixed outline). Not while the panels float in a narrow window.

props.name: resizeStep
props.description: One arrow-key step on a resize handle, a CSS length such as "1rem" (default 8px); four steps with Shift.

props.name: endWidth
props.description: The end panel's width, controlled: a CSS length such as "30rem", or unset for its opening width. Pass with `onEndResize`.

props.name: onEndResize
props.description: Reports the end panel's new width as it is resized, in rem to a sixteenth (`undefined`: back to its opening width). `done` is false while a drag is under way and true when it ends or a key sets it: keep the width then (for the next visit). With it, the layout holds no width of its own for the end panel: pass `endWidth`.

props.name: endMin
props.description: The narrowest the end panel can be dragged, such as "24rem" (default the least of `c.editor-layout.panel-min` and its opening width).

props.name: resizeValueText
props.description: Words a screen reader says for a resize handle's width, given the width in px, such as "24 rem wide" (default none: the number alone).

props.name: toggles
props.description: With panel heads (no bar), where an open panel's toggle sits in its head: `outer` (default) at the window's edge; `inner` at the edge beside the working area, level with the head's first row (Figma UI3's layers toggle); `none`: no panel toggles at all, for a studio whose panels are always docked (pass `startOpen` and `endOpen` true); a floating panel's Escape doesn't close it, since nothing would open it again.

props.name: startSize
props.description: The start panel's opening width, a CSS length such as "16rem" (default the theme's `c.editor-layout.panel-start`).

props.name: endSize
props.description: The end panel's opening width, a CSS length such as "41rem" for a two-column inspector (default the theme's `c.editor-layout.panel-end`).

props.name: endMax
props.description: The widest the end panel can be, opened or dragged (default the theme's `c.editor-layout.panel-max`, 30 rem). Set it with an `endSize` above 30 rem.

props.name: workMin
props.description: The narrowest the working area gets while both panels are docked, such as "24rem". The end panel gives way first, down to `c.editor-layout.panel-min`, so it is never wider than the room minus the start panel and this; a resizable panel can't be dragged wider than that either. Default: no floor.

props.name: workFill
props.description: LR72 (opt-in): what's put in the working area takes its full width (and height), whatever it is: a screen of content, a loading state's wrapper. Off, a child sizes itself (a Canvas or ScrollArea already fills it).

props.name: endFill
props.description: LR104 (opt-in): the end panel's content fills the panel from top to bottom (an inspector): its content area takes the panel's height and what's in it grows to fill it (with Tabs `fill` and SectionedForm `fill` down the chain).

settings.description: A resize handle's hit width, centred on the panel's inner edge (default 0.5rem). Set var(--space-4) for an editor whose inspector edge is a wide, quiet strip (LR77).
The line a resize handle shows only while hovered, focused or dragged (default color.focus). Set var(--color-accent) to draw it in the accent (LR77).
